correctness.rationale: For each \(u,v\), the two determinant equations have \(M(u,v)=q^2(q^2-1)+q^4\mathbf1_{\{u=v=0\}}\) sextuples. The \(w\)-functional has rank one except for exactly \(q^2\) exceptional sextuples at \(u=v=0\), where it has rank zero. Two unrestricted central coordinates give the exact three-case formula. The group commutator shifts \(w\) by \(-(a+A)v\) and thus has identical fibers; this is proved by the direct group-matrix identity. Counts sum to \(q^{12}\) and are positive in every characteristic. The checker exhaustively verifies group and Lie targets at \(q=2,3\) and first-layer identities in \(\mathbf F_4\); finite computation supports but does not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: Naik (arXiv:1805.00091v2, Theorem 1.4) proves nonidentity uniformity only for class-three groups with two conjugacy-class sizes, a hypothesis not satisfied by UT_4. Kaur et al. (arXiv:2006.01493v1, Sections 6,8) compute commuting tuple probabilities and thereby the zero fiber, but not all prescribed nonzero fibers. Published Kronecker path-algebra commutator results treat a different square-zero-radical multiplication. The new nonzero law gives two levels, not one, in a canonical class-three family for every finite field. Broad hidden equivalences remain possible.
residual_risks: The complete 2015 Nath–Yadav paper was unavailable; its abstract restricts attention to two-conjugacy-size groups, but hidden broader implications are not completely excluded.
A more general commutator distribution under word-map, orbit, character-theoretic or isoclinism terminology could subsume the nonzero counts despite absence in the inspected primary sources.

Kaur et al. 2020 arXiv v1 contains an apparent internal inconsistency between its first branching column and its Section 8 cp_2 entry; this finding derives its own zero fiber without relying on either printed probability formula.

value.rationale: The set of nonidentity commutator fiber sizes is an explicitly studied invariant of probabilistic group theory (Naik 2018). This result classifies every target fiber for a natural class-three group family over infinitely many finite fields, proves the unexpected exact factor-two disparity between nonidentity central and noncentral commutators, extends uniformly to even characteristic, and identifies an identical distribution for the associated nilpotent Lie algebra. Its scientific content is the complete nonzero distribution, not a small numerical adjustment to an averaged commuting probability.
